post_title: Why am I getting double horizontal Internal Lines?
post_details: Hello, can someone explain why Im getting double horizontal Internal Lines? Or what could provoke that? thanks in regards
post_description: The purpose of this web page is to provide insights and solutions for understanding and resolving the issue of double horizontal internal lines in design or layout configurations.

comments.comment_body: "can someone explain why Im getting double horizontal Internal Lines?": looks like you're currently offsetting 2 lines (left and right for top and bottom) that are both in-line with each other and their segment points aren't parallel. You're seeing two lines because they are angled which is making the crisscross shape. they are extending to the pattern outline and creating the X shape you're seeing. (this would have happened with them being parallel anyway btw, they would have been layered over each other instead) "what could provoke that?": selecting Two horizontal (angled) lines that are parallel to each other being selected with the dialog box option checked being EXTEND &gt pattern outline. hope that helps!

comments.comment_body: Hi 27594521774361, it could be from a couple of reasons. The most common are 1) the Line lengths between the shapes are not the same (example- the square's circumference is a lot smaller than the surrounding pattern's measurements) 2) there is pressure value in the patterns: allowing the items to inflate and pressure allows for materials with different properties to stretch &amp deform in different ways which can result in different responses. 3) The strengthen feature (the orange color in the window) prevents stretching and "strengthens" the material. That could remove any stretching happening which is why you are seeing that

post_details: Hello! New to MD and have gone through a myriad of tutorials but still struggling to get my bearings regarding the best production workflow from Maya to MD to Maya. Couple part (hopefully not dumb) question, so bear with me: - How have others dealt with thickness once back in Maya? If clothing created in MD is rather thick (think like .5cm thick wool/felt hats and coats) having that in the simulation/export makes more sense to me but I've seen others mention save it out thin and apply thickness in the 3D software. To my knowledge, extrude in Maya doesn't add thickness evenly to both sides the same way MD would. - Related to point above, how have others dealt with UVs in these cases where you'd ultimately need/want the side and back of the thicker fabric to have their own unique UVs (not just the fronts represented)? - It seems retopologizing and saving out both your tri high detail simulated mesh from MD as well as a lower res quad mesh to smooth and transfer attributes in Maya is a more preferred method from what I've seen. Is this the case for others that use this workflow?
post_description: This webpage aims to facilitate discussion and share best practices among users navigating the workflow between Maya and Marvelous Designer (MD), specifically addressing challenges related to fabric thickness, UV mapping, and mesh retopology.

comments.comment_body: Hi Jessica - Dealing with thickness. Clothes with thickness will be expressed as extra geometry to simulate the thickness expression from MD when exported as FBX. As thickness is not a value that can be transferred with maps or FBX, the UVs will be autogenerated based on the layer it has been created. - For the UVs for the inner layer, I recommend Layer Clone (Under/Over) so they are another layer with their UVs. As said above if you use a single layer, the UVs of the front will be replicated and used for the extra geometry created when exporting the file as FBX. - Exporting High and low-res garments is part of the baking process. You can do that process in any software of your choice once you have high and low.
Thank you! This helps a lot.
